headline: An energy-supply shock on top of 5% long yields
analysis: Three things dominate this page: WTI spot 88% above where the year started, a 10-year yield of about 5% against CPI inflation of 3.4%, and a record 65 armed conflicts. They are linked in the data, but loosely. Oil moves with yields and against stocks, gold has followed yields rather than conflict, and equities have so far absorbed both, with the S&P 500 under 2% below its record close.
evidence: Scorecard; headline tiles; conflict cards; news panel

headline: Oil is the transmission channel
analysis: WTI averaged 58.0 in December 2025, 91.4 in March and 102.1 in May, dipped to 80.5 in July and was back at 97.3 in September. The Brent minus WTI spot spread is 7.33 dollars, wider than on 85% of days since 2016 (median 3.96), and the futures gap on 26 Oct was 14.05. That pattern fits a supply-risk premium on seaborne crude; news reports tie Brent to Middle East attacks on Saudi infrastructure. I have not tested causation.
evidence: Oil chart; Brent minus WTI chart; scorecard; news panel

headline: Oil and yields move together, but only loosely
analysis: The correlation of monthly changes is +0.31 over 60 months and +0.40 over the last 12, so oil explains roughly 10% to 16% of yield moves. Oil this month barely predicts next month's yield change (+0.17), so the link is coincident, not a lead. CPI inflation fell from 4.25% in May to 3.4% in August and has flattened, but the September oil average was 16% above August's, a risk to the next prints.
evidence: Correlation table; rolling correlation; CPI chart

headline: Stocks look more oil-sensitive lately
analysis: The oil and S&P 500 correlation moved from -0.14 over 60 months to -0.44 over the last 12 (24-month: -0.13). That is only 12 observations, so read it as a direction. Even so, the S&P 500 closed at 7,676.77 on 26 Oct, 1.8% below its 6 Oct record close of 7,818.93, and the VIX at 18.39 sits inside its 52-week range of 13.38 to 35.30.
evidence: Correlation table; S&P and VIX charts; news panel

headline: Gold has traded as a rates asset, not a conflict hedge
analysis: Gold's correlation with the 10-year yield is -0.29 over 60 months and -0.40 over 12, against 0.00 and -0.09 with oil and +0.14 and +0.11 with stocks. Spot gold is 17.8% below its Q1 2026 average despite record conflict. The dollar is up against EUR (3.7%), JPY (2.7%) and INR (8.1%) over a year but flat to GBP (-0.4%) and down against CNY (-6.3%), so I would not lean on a dollar explanation.
evidence: Correlation table; gold charts; FX card

headline: Industrial-leaning metals are falling harder than gold
analysis: Against Q1 2026 averages, silver is down 36.4%, platinum 31.7% and gold 17.8%; palladium is down 18.9% since 27 Sep. The gold to silver ratio rose from 58.0 in Q1 2026 to 75.1. That is consistent with weaker industrial demand or a positioning unwind in silver; the data cannot separate the two.
evidence: Metals charts; gold to silver ratio

headline: Real yields are firm, the curve is not inverted
analysis: The approximate real 10-year yield (10-year minus CPI) was 1.28 points in August, higher than 68% of months since 2006 but far below the 5.66 peak of July 2009. If inflation holds at 3.4%, September's 4.99% implies about 1.6. The 10-year auction yield rose from 4.580% in July to 5.300% in October (+72 basis points), and the 26 Oct 2-year auction covered 2.59 times against an average of 2.64. With the 10-year 0.31 points above the 2-year, the curve points to inflation and term-premium pressure rather than imminent recession.
evidence: Real yield chart; yield curve; auction table and trend

headline: Conflict intensity and market relevance differ
analysis: There are 65 state-based conflicts, a record, including 8 interstate (4 in 2024) and 14 in the Middle East, also a record. Europe has one conflict (Ukraine) but 61.7% of battle deaths. Markets are reacting to the Middle East, not to Europe's deadliest war, plausibly because of the oil chokepoints involved. That is a hypothesis; the dashboard shows the pieces, not a tested link.
evidence: Conflict cards; conflict intensity table; oil charts

headline: A record clean build alongside an oil spike
analysis: Solar added 511.2 GW and wind 158.7 GW in 2025, the largest annual additions in the series. Oil above 100 dollars improves the relative economics of renewables, but nothing here measures power prices, so treat the link as a hypothesis.

headline: Climate and nuclear risks are not in the market data
analysis: CO2 was 2.07 ppm higher than a year earlier in August and the 12-month mean temperature anomaly is 1.04 C. FAS estimates 12,187 nuclear warheads, with military stockpiles rising again, and describes New START as now expired. None of these shows up in the price series, and I found no short-term link.

headline: Near-term triggers
analysis: The Fed decision on 28 Oct; the 5-year and 7-year auctions on 27 and 29 Oct; whether the 10-year holds below 5%; the gap between oil futures and spot; and whether stocks' oil sensitivity persists. A break in the gold and yield relationship would also change the read on gold.

headline: Limits of the evidence
analysis: The correlations use monthly changes over 60 and 12 observations and do not prove causes. The oil spot series ends 20 Oct while the tiles use futures. Metals daily data comes from an aggregator. Several series have a single source (see Data quality). I have not seen the dashboard render.
